title: Original small queue FIFO, strict removal and input recovery
oracle: Literal FIFO/peek/length/first-strict-removal expectations, NaN indexOf characterization, real returned-object reference histories, source-derived malformed-list native errors before insertion with unchanged state and retry, typed view byte tables, and immutable external sequence-model expectations for generated state histories.

trials.execution: Executed partial original queue behavior against actual archived sources at 1051710191 and 1051908825 through the local core Subject: 13 cases, 440 probes per revision, unchanged comparisons; 14 tests passed. Complete results were retained privately before assertions. Explicit diagnostic process mode reports isolated:false; large-list coverage is five prefix values plus counts, with no full-tail, external-callback or mid-prefix-failure proof.
trials.sourceScope: Actual default-unwrapped SmallQueue constructor via $module and public methods only. Native source Array.forEach callback executes actual enqueue code; no supplied callback/helper/private array or provider.
trials.identityScope: Actual peek/dequeue returned objects are retained for strict reference remove, reenqueue and identity; fresh equal records do not match. No argument-retention or arbitrary property seam.
trials.failureScope: Selected lists without callable forEach throw native TypeError before first insertion; existing count/head and valid retries remain observable. No fabricated mid-prefix failure.
trials.largeInputScope: 2048-item list assertions observe initial length, five-item literal prefix and remaining count/nonempty only; no full unobserved-tail equality claim.
trials.domains: Inputs, values, lengths and histories remain unbounded; finite generated/literal samples do not establish exhaustive domains, persistence, restart or security/copy ownership.
